technical_and_design_decisions: Use Go programming language for implementation, aligning with existing fabric-config library.
Follow existing API patterns in the library for consistency, such as using similar function signatures for add/remove operations.
For U3, make the top-level OrdererAddresses field non-updatable and only support a removal function to enforce migration to orderer org endpoints.
For U5, ensure consenter removal matches all four fields (host, port, client_tls_cert, server_tls_cert) for safe and precise removal.
For U6, implement the CLI tool with JSON input parsing, support for connection profile and signing identities, and a dry-run mode for previewing updates.
For U7 and U8, maintain backward compatibility by preserving existing Get/Set functions and adding new individual update functions as separate paths.
Design API functions to handle error cases and validate inputs, such as certificate validation for MSP updates.
Use unit tests and integration tests to ensure reliability and correctness of new features.
assumptions: The existing fabric-config library codebase is available and accessible for modification.
Development environment includes Go toolchain and necessary dependencies (e.g., Fabric libraries) are set up.
No major changes to the underlying Hyperledger Fabric core libraries are required, only client-side API enhancements.
The specification is complete and detailed enough to proceed without further clarifications.
Testing will use standard Go testing frameworks and mock data for validation.
The developer is familiar with the fabric-config library architecture and Hyperledger Fabric configuration concepts.
Effort estimates are based on a single developer working full-time on these activities.

activities.activity_description: Review the specification, design API changes, plan implementation approach, set up development environment, and outline test strategies.
Develop function to add a new consortium to the consortiums group, handle implications for empty consortiums, and update examples to demonstrate consortium and org addition.

activities.activity_name: Implement U2: Config Update Without Signing Identities
activities.activity_description: Modify config update generation to return a cb.ConfigUpdateEnvelope without requiring signing identities, allowing later signing via peer commands.

activities.activity_name: Implement U3: Remove Legacy Orderer Addresses
activities.activity_description: Add function RemoveLegacyOrdererAddresses to remove top-level orderer addresses, and update genesis block creation to exclude this field, requiring orderer org endpoints.
Develop function to remove the KafkaBrokers section from config to support migration from Kafka to EtcdRaft.
Create functions to add and remove consenters from etcdraft orderer configuration, ensuring safe removal by matching host, port, and both certificates.

activities.activity_name: Develop CLI Tool for Bulk Operations (U6)
activities.activity_description: Build a CLI tool that accepts JSON input for bulk operations on channels, supports operations like consenter updates, MSP updates, anchor peer management, dry-run mode, connection profile, and signing identities.

activities.activity_name: Implement U7: Individual Orderer Configuration Updates
activities.activity_description: Add API functions for OrdererGroup to update individual fields like MaxMessageCount, BatchTimeout, etc., following existing patterns and preserving other values.

activities.activity_name: Implement U8: Individual MSP Configuration Updates
activities.activity_description: Develop API functions for OrdererOrgGroup, ApplicationOrgGroup, and ConsortiumOrgGroup to update individual MSP fields such as adding/removing certs, setting crypto config, etc.

activities.activity_name: Write Unit Tests for New Features
activities.activity_description: Create comprehensive unit tests for all new functions in U1-U8 and the CLI tool, covering edge cases and validation logic.
Update existing examples to demonstrate new API functions, add documentation for the CLI tool, and ensure clarity in usage.
Integrate all changes, perform end-to-end testing with sample channels, and conduct code reviews to ensure quality and adherence to standards.
